findings.title: The RT-4 fix replaced one false comment with another: the test does NOT discriminate an own-connection helper, and a planted own-connection mutation SURVIVES
findings.arbiter_reasoning: M10: writeRefusalEvent's INSERT and its occurredAtFragment were rerouted onto a freshly constructed postgres.js client (`postgres(process.env.DATABASE_POOL_URL, { max: 1, idle_timeout: 1 })`) instead of the caller's `tx`. Baseline green (1 executed, 10 skipped). Under the mutant the case still PASSED (1 executed, 10 skipped). NOT equivalent: the mutation changes the helper from the caller's deciding transaction to an independent connection, which is exactly the invariant #15 violation the new comment names, and in the general case a successful insert on that connection commits independently of the caller's rollback. NOT unexecuted: the mutated line is the very INSERT this fixture forces to fail. It survives only because the fixture forces a CHECK violation (an invalid refusal_category), so no row is produced on EITHER connection and nothing can survive the rollback — which is precisely why the assertion cannot see the difference. Round 1 had already recorded this in prose ('the forced insert fails on either connection and leaves nothing behind either way'); the fix deleted the catch half and PROMOTED the connection half into a positive coverage claim. Rated P1 rather than P0 because the production code is correct, M9b proves the case is not a could-not-fail test, and the likeliest real form of the defect (importing @/lib/db/server) is mechanically blocked by ci:db-imports strict; note however that ci:db-imports matches only the db/server specifier, so a direct `postgres(...)` construction inside src/lib/refusals/ is caught by nothing today.

findings.title: The new Governor alert row calls an email-only route 'not a gap' inside a section whose stated premise is that email is not an acceptable route

Non-email paging route (mandatory)', whose second sentence is 'Alerts must reach a non-email channel because admin email shares the Resend provider with the product' (:25-26).
